one_line: Incident war room with phase-gated WebMCP capabilities and human escalation.

leverage_rationale: The core safety model is that unauthorized capabilities do not exist in the page's current tool surface, rather than relying on an agent instruction to refuse them. Shared incident state and human approval are central.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly says tools appear and disappear with incident phase.
About text describes rollback absent in triage, request_escalation, named human approval, toolchange, and automatic withdrawal of write access.
Devpost preview visibly shows incident timeline, tool call ledger, and WebMCP control panel.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent incident-console concept and a substantial prototype view, but no submitted video/frame sequence is actually available despite frame-sheet paths, so end-to-end execution remains claimed.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows metrics, shared incident timeline, tool call ledger, and WebMCP panel.
About text specifies phase transitions, confirmations, and mitigation flow.
Frame sheets are repetitive and small; no readable end-to-end result is verified.
impact_rationale: Production incident response has a clear audience and a serious need for constrained agent assistance; phase-aware capability gating directly addresses the safety objection to autonomous rollback.
impact_evidence: About text identifies engineering teams and 3am incident work.
Read-only investigation versus human-approved rollback is a credible operational distinction.
creativity_rationale: Treating permission as dynamic tool existence, with the incident phase recomputing the agent surface, is a memorable and well-developed WebMCP interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Tool surface changes on phase transitions.
Agent can withdraw its own write access after mitigation.
Timeline and tool ledger make shared reasoning visible.
usability_note: The shown war-room layout is information-dense but organized around metrics, timeline, and tool activity; small evidence limits detailed usability assessment.
red_flags: No actual video evidence or transcript; frame-sheet evidence is repetitive and difficult to read.
Execution is based largely on claims and one packaging screenshot.
standouts: Capability nonexistence is used as the safety boundary.
Human escalation is represented as a concrete tool-surface transition, not just a prompt rule.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and a strong safety-oriented product concept; advance despite execution evidence being incomplete.

one_line: Deterministic crisis simulator where AI proposes interventions and a human decides.

leverage_rationale: The simulation exposes structured causal state and lets an agent investigate, compare interventions, and stage plans while the human controls execution; pixel-level UI driving would be substantially less reliable for this complex state.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and about text explicitly describe WebMCP investigation, structured city state, root-cause tracing, forecasting, and staged plans.

execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent simulation concept, multiple missions, live city views, and a clear propose-review-decide loop; stills and claims do not fully prove the simulation's end-to-end behavior.

Devpost preview shows intervention options, predicted impacts, and explicit human approval.

impact_rationale: Emergency planners, learners, and decision-makers can plausibly benefit from a deterministic exercise that makes cascading consequences and human accountability visible; the packet demonstrates the intended value clearly.
impact_evidence: About text names exposed residents, injuries, untreated cases, fatalities, hospital load, travel time, and incident resolution.
Human remains final authority and simulation never directly executes.

usability_note: The staged plan review and visible consequence comparison are understandable, though the dense simulator UI may require learning.
red_flags: No transcript and frame text is often small.
Some execution details rely on description rather than directly readable frames.
standouts: Deterministic baseline comparison makes AI recommendations inspectable.
advance_reason: One of the strongest packets: high WebMCP leverage, distinctive simulation concept, and credible human-accountability workflow.

one_line: Trust layer that preserves evidence, policy, and state across agent handoffs.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP tools expose application-owned state, receipts, revision gates, and verification across changing agent contexts; the product's core promise depends on structured shared state that generic UI automation cannot safely reproduce.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies read_incident, submit_handoff, read_handoff, run_verification, and submit_resolution.
Closure is rejected with VERIFICATION_REQUIRED until an application-owned checkout test passes.
Devpost preview visibly shows live application state, revision, awaiting verification, and closure rejected.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete synthetic checkout incident and the frame sheets show a multi-stage recovery workflow with handoff, gate decision, and verification states; direct video evidence is absent, so some completion remains claimed.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets visibly show Checkout recovery and changing three-step workflow states.
Devpost screenshot shows Revision 2, AWAITING VERIFICATION, closure rejection, and handoff timeline.
About text describes successor resume, verification receipt, and committed revision.
impact_rationale: Long-running agent workflows need reliable handoffs, auditability, and protection against confident false completion; the synthetic checkout case makes the operational value concrete.
impact_evidence: About text identifies silent drift and false completion as failure modes.
Human-defined closure rule and exportable audit record directly address trust and governance.
creativity_rationale: Making the application—not the model—the authority for state, policy, evidence, and completion is an original and deeply pursued agent-workflow model.
creativity_evidence: Predecessor summary is explicitly labeled untrusted.
Source-set hashes, evidence identifiers, receipts, and revision binding form a coherent trust chain.
Arrastra visualization is tied to the audit workflow rather than decorative animation.
usability_note: The recovery timeline and gate states communicate why work cannot close, though the dense operational model may be specialized.
red_flags: No video transcript; frame sheets are repeated and small.
Synthetic checkout may not represent a production integration, though that is appropriate to the demo scope.
standouts: Application-owned verification gate prevents false completion.
Strong evidence/provenance model across agent handoffs.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage, strong execution evidence, and a compelling trust problem; clear advance.
